conviction_note: My four findings net to roughly zero on a $117bn name with a 4.57% event-implied move; the small negative comes from the one thing the baseline mis-states — its put/call OI ratio of 2.37 reads defensive, while the actual pre-print option flow is heavily call-side and the stock is +9.6% off its mid-July level with a published sell-side 'beat and raise' (Needham PT $101 to $114), which is the exact setup in which MDT's own record is 2 up / 5 down and in which both August-2025 and February-2026 beats were sold.

findings.finding: The syndicated Q1 FY27 consensus revenue of $9.47bn (+10.4% on the $8,578m year-ago base) sits roughly a point below what Medtronic's own 3 June quarterly guidance implies — 11.5% to 12.0% organic growth plus a 'neutral to $50 million' FX tailwind plus acquired revenue from CathWorks/Scientia/SPR, i.e. about $9.55-9.65bn — while consensus EPS of $1.39 is exactly the midpoint of the guided $1.38-$1.40; the same one-point gap exists at the full-year level ($38.85bn consensus vs 6.75-7.25% organic on $36,364m plus 0-1% FX plus M&A). The likeliest cause is incomplete modelling of the 53rd selling week, which management sized at 500-600bps of Q1 revenue but 600-700bps of Q1 EPS, so the EPS line was captured and part of the revenue line was not. Mechanically this makes a print that merely lands on guidance read in the wire copy as a $100-180m top-line beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody publishes the reconciliation of a consensus print against the company's own quarterly guide, and the inconsistency is visible only as an internal contradiction in the estimate set (EPS on guidance, revenue below it). If it were priced, previews would be flagging a 'low bar on revenue' rather than quoting the $9.47bn as the bar; instead Zacks' preview quotes it straight. I keep the size small and let the band cross zero because the marginal holder of a mega-cap trades the buy-side bar, not the Zacks bar, and MDT has twice in the last four prints sold off on a headline beat.
findings.independence: Overlaps only in direction with the Needham note (PT $101 to $114, expects a beat and a guidance raise, https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/needham-raises-medtronic-stock-price-target-on-product-cycle-93CH-4879312); the arithmetic itself is independent of any broker note and rests on the transcript plus the $8,578m base in the 2025-08-19 release.

findings.finding: As of 2026-08-31 no registration statement or tender-offer document for the MiniMed split-off exists on EDGAR: Medtronic (CIK 1613103) has filed no 8-K since 2026-06-03 and no S-4/Schedule TO, and MiniMed Group (CIK 2062583) shows no S-4, S-1, 425 or SC TO on or after 2026-06-01. On 3 June management said separation was expected 'prior to year-end' and explicitly framed early separation as potential upside to FY27 guidance, which assumes twelve months of Diabetes consolidation. An exchange offer needs a registered offer document and a ~20-business-day offer period, so with nothing on file at end-August the 'upside from early separation' has not begun to be executed. Compounding it, MMED traded at $18.92 on 2026-08-26, below its $20.00 March IPO price, which weakens the discount economics of a split-off and raises the odds of a plain pro-rata spin-off that would retire none of Medtronic's ~1.28bn shares.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an absence, and absences do not generate wire copy — there is no article saying 'Medtronic has not yet filed the exchange-offer S-4'. If the market had priced a slip, previews would be discussing whether FY27 guidance gets re-based rather than repeating the June 'full twelve months of Diabetes' framing. The band crosses zero because the standard sequencing is to launch an exchange offer immediately after a quarterly release, so the same fact can flip to a positive on 1 September.
findings.independence: Cross-checked against Medtronic's own EDGAR index (no 8-K since 2026-06-03, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001613103&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=60) and against the 2026-08-17 DEF 14A, whose only capital resolution is the routine annual 'overseas market purchases' authority, with no off-market purchase or exchange-offer resolution for the 15 October AGM.

findings.finding: The Investor Day Medtronic committed to on 2025-08-19, when it added two Elliott-adjacent directors and formed the Growth and Operating Committees, was promised for 'mid-calendar year 2026' and was to lay out the go-forward financial algorithm and the committees' margin and efficiency targets. Mid-2026 has passed and, as of 2026-08-31, no date has been announced: the June Q4 call did not mention it and the Medtronic newsroom shows only three releases since (21 July Touch Surgery Aide, 6 August Affera CE Mark, 20 August dividend).
findings.why_not_priced: A missed soft deadline on an event with no announced date produces no headline and no estimate revision, so there is nothing for the tape to have reflected. If it were priced you would see notes handicapping the margin target, as happened around every peer's activist-driven capital markets day. The 1 September call is the natural venue to set a date, so the sign is genuinely two-sided and the band is wide.
findings.independence: Independent of the other findings. Corroborated only by absence: the Medtronic newsroom listing through 2026-08-20 (https://news.medtronic.com/) contains no Investor Day announcement.

findings.finding: Boston Scientific reported on 2026-07-29 that its electrophysiology business grew only 3% in the US in calendar Q2 2026 (versus 23% internationally), citing competitive pressure and noting that US PFA is now roughly 80% of the AFib market. Calendar Q2 covers about two-thirds of Medtronic's fiscal Q1 (25 April to 31 July), and Cardiac Ablation Solutions — up 78% globally and 124% in the US in Medtronic's Q4 FY26 — is the single largest contributor to the 6.75-7.25% FY27 organic guide. The datapoint reads as continued Affera/Sphere-9 share gain in the quarter Medtronic is about to report, but the same disclosure caps how much market growth is left.
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced, and I am sizing it accordingly. MDT rose 3.2% on 27-28 July, i.e. before the BSX print, and only 0.8% on 29 July itself, so the tape does not look like it repriced Medtronic's CAS line on the read-across. But the 80%-penetration remark is the bearish half of the same disclosure and cuts the other way, which is exactly why a single number here is not worth more than a few tenths.
findings.independence: Overlaps with nothing else I found; the Affera CE Mark expansion for ventricular arrhythmias on 2026-08-06 (https://news.medtronic.com/) points the same way on the franchise but is a European label, not a US volume datapoint.

searched_and_found_nothing: FX as a guidance-revision lever: the FY27 guide was set on 'recent rates' as of 3 June 2026 (neutral to 1% accretive on revenue), and the dollar has barely moved since — DXY around 99.4 on 3 June against about 99.5 now, EURUSD 1.1567 to 1.1612 — so there is no FX-driven raise or cut hiding here (Yahoo chart v8 for DX-Y.NYB and EURUSD=X, fetched 2026-08-31)
Quiet 8-K: Medtronic has filed no 8-K at all since 2026-06-03, so there is no unnoticed material event on file
New M&A: no Medtronic acquisition announced after the 20 May 2026 SPR Therapeutics deal, so the '2% M&A dilution' assumption in the FY27 guide is unchanged
Tariffs: the Section 232 medical devices/supplies investigation opened 24 September 2025 is still unresolved as of August 2026, so the $250m FY27 / $75m Q1 COGS assumption has no new input either way

Recalls: the August 2026 Class I recall of DLP Left Heart Vent Catheters covers about 101,000 units of a low-revenue cannula line and already produced the 2.2% drop on 27 August; the 348,616-unit ICD/CRT-D glassed-feedthrough recall that surfaces in search is a May 2023 action, not new
IRS transfer-pricing litigation: no Tax Court decision on the Eighth Circuit remand has issued, so no new contingency
MiniMed as an early read on the Diabetes line: MMED reports the same morning at 3:45 a.m. PDT, so there is no pre-print information there
Layoffs and WARN: only the 81-person Northridge diabetes cut (notice 5 February 2026) and the previously announced Santa Rosa wind-down through spring 2028; no new restructuring signal
Proxy for separation mechanics: the 2026-08-17 DEF 14A lists six routine resolutions for the 15 October AGM and no off-market purchase authority that a split-off exchange offer would need

Executive turnover: Brett Wall's Neuroscience exit (effective handover to 1 September 2026) and Jason Weidman's departure to Teleflex are both already reported; no unreported Form 4 cluster or officer departure found
baseline_tension: The baseline's own put/call open-interest ratio of 2.37 reads defensive and is the number I most disagree with: the flat 25-delta skew of -0.21 and the reported pre-print flow (roughly ten calls per put, with 18,801 of the $100 September calls traded against 1,704 open interest) say the marginal option buyer is positioning for upside into a stock that has run 9.6% off its mid-July low, which means my one positive finding — a low headline revenue bar — is the half of my work most likely to be already in the price, and my negative findings (no split-off document, no Investor Day date) are the half nobody has written down.
